entries.title: Ten Cameras, 5.1 Million Police Searches | Utah Civic Compact
entries.metaDescription: Weber County, Utah operates ten license plate reader cameras. Records released under GRAMA show 3,343 law enforcement agencies in 45 states ran 5,171,087 searches against them between February 2022 and July 2026 — 96.6% from outside Utah.
entries.ogTitle: Ten cameras in one Utah county were searched 5.1 million times by police in 45 states
entries.ogDescription: Records Weber County released under GRAMA show 3,343 law enforcement agencies ran 5,171,087 searches against its license plate reader networks. Weber County's own deputies ran 13,100 of them.

entries.title: If Weber County Followed the Law, How Did This Happen? | Utah Civic Compact
entries.metaDescription: Utah has some of the strongest ALPR laws in the country. This policy paper asks whether those laws describe the system Utah agencies actually purchased — reading the Utah Code against the Weber County–Flock Safety contract, clause by clause.
entries.ogTitle: If Weber County Followed the Law, How Did This Happen?
entries.ogDescription: Utah's ALPR statute governs a plate reader, run by a governmental entity, holding its own data. What was sold was a right of access to a web interface and ten more cameras on a private network. A policy paper by Jarom Gillins, Director of Policy.

entries.title: The Stratos Project: MIDA Violated State Law | Utah Civic Compact
entries.metaDescription: Utah Civic Compact documents how MIDA violated Utah Code § 63H-1 in approving Kevin O'Leary's 9-gigawatt natural gas data center in Box Elder County — including a fabricated county consent date and a welfare finding made before any impact studies began.
entries.ogTitle: The Stratos Project: MIDA Violated State Law | Utah Civic Compact
entries.ogDescription: Utah Civic Compact documents how MIDA broke three provisions of Utah law fast-tracking a 9-gigawatt natural gas data center in Box Elder County — including a fabricated county consent date and a welfare finding made before any impact studies began.
